statements.proposition: The change is backward compatible: it has no effect on behaviour when BASE_URL has no path.
statements.label: FALSE
statements.note: Concrete check settles it. The change calls get_path_prefix() (which calls get_settings(), which caches the settings globally) at import time at the end of bugsink/settings/default.py. User configs (conf_templates/singleserver.py.template, development.py) do 'from bugsink.settings.default import *' and only afterwards define BUGSINK = {...}, so the cached settings are built from defaults alone and the user's BUGSINK dict (including BASE_URL and SITE_TITLE) is ignored. This happens whether or not BASE_URL has a path, so there is an impact (regression) with no-path BASE_URL. Reproduced with a minimal conf at head vs base.
evidence: gh api pulls/200: base 5307860b, head 42bcd5d9; bugsink/settings/default.py +7 adds module-level 'from bugsink.app_settings import get_path_prefix; _path_prefix = get_path_prefix()'
bugsink/app_settings.py get_settings() caches in global _settings on first call, reading getattr(django.conf.settings,'BUGSINK',{})
bugsink/conf_templates/singleserver.py.template line 4 'from bugsink.settings.default import *' then BUGSINK = {...} at line 80

Sandboxed run, conf = 'from bugsink.settings.default import *; BUGSINK={SITE_TITLE:CUSTOM, BASE_URL:https://example.com}' (no path): at base prints 'TITLE CUSTOM BASE https://example.com'; at head prints 'TITLE Bugsink BASE http://localhost:8000' (user config ignored)
